### SPEC-004 correction: `rust-version`/`license` fixed for michi adoption

Post-gate, post-implementation correction via `canon/correct`, triggered by the michi
integration research below. Two of AC-020's nine locked `[workspace.package]` values were
wrong: `license = "MIT"` (the repo's actual `LICENSE` file was already AGPL-3.0 — an
internal inconsistency in the source doc, unrelated to michi) and `rust-version = "1.85"`
(michi, now a confirmed dependency, needs 1.96). Corrected to `AGPL-3.0-or-later` / `1.96`,
an intentional, explicitly-flagged divergence from `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md`'s
own literal text — canon-verifier confirmed the source document genuinely still says the
old values, so this isn't silently drifting from spec, it's a stated, gated exception.
canon-auditor caught the correction's own blast radius: the `scope` field's blanket "all
verbatim per Section 28" claim wasn't updated alongside AC-020, so it briefly contradicted
the criterion it was supposed to summarize — fixed. `vector-planner` amended `PLAN-004`
(only T-001 owns AC-020) and, checking for incidental damage, found two more:
`T-006`/`T-023` had hardcoded `rust_version=='1.85'`/`license=='MIT'` assertions baked into
otherwise-unrelated `cargo metadata` checks — not their own criteria, but would have
produced false failures on any future re-run. Fixed both. `vector-challenger`'s review of
the amended T-001 found real shell bugs of its own: the primary "nothing else moved" diff
was guaranteed to fail (comparing against a 14-line expectation when the real file already
had 67 lines of later tasks' content committed), its offered fallback was an elided `...`
wrapped around a `head | diff -` construct that starves `diff` of a second operand, and a
dangling reference told the implementer to fall back to "T-001's original pre-amendment
steps" — which no longer existed in the plan at all. All fixed, each fix independently
executed against the real repo before trusting it. `lambda-implementer` re-ran the
corrected T-001 clean — commit `414225b`.

plan@1 (`PLAN-004.json`); two independent `vector-challenger` rounds found and fixed 13 issues

`lambda-implementer` outright; a verification gap where the plan's biggest blocks of transcribed
content — the 10 later dependency version pins and all of `lib.rs` — were never diffed against
the source document, only counted; a BSD `wc -l` padding bug in a length guard my own fix
introduced; a broken backtick-in-markdown assertion; a missing cwd anchor). Third round: clean
pass.

`lambda-recon` → 23 `lambda-implementer` task dispatches (one per task, strict no-batching) →
`lambda-mutator` → `lambda-exit-gate`, all in sequence. Root `Cargo.toml`, `crates/monokl/Cargo.toml`,
and `crates/monokl/src/lib.rs` now exist and are byte-exact against `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md`,
confirmed via pattern-anchored diffs (not hardcoded line ranges) with working length guards.

tasks), all 28 acceptance criteria evidenced, `lambda-exit-gate` independently re-ran the

confirmed zero mutable code paths (expected — `lib.rs` is bare module declarations, no function
bodies; both `Cargo.toml`s are non-code TOML) by isolating `lib.rs` into a synthetic crate and
running `cargo mutants --list` against it (0 candidates), not by assuming the tool had nothing to do.

**Known, deliberate, already-locked gap (AC-008B): the real workspace cannot `cargo build`/`cargo test` yet.**
`io-errors` (a dependency `MonoklError` needs) is pinned to a private registry (`registry =

# Proposed michi adjustments, surfaced during monokl integration research

Context for whoever picks this up in the michi repo: monokl (a sibling orin-axi tool) is
doing its first real integration pass against michi. Two research passes read michi's
actual source end-to-end (not just docs) and one deep architectural-fit pass (opus,
compiled and ran real probes against michi 0.1.0) checked whether michi's types map
cleanly onto monokl's already-locked domain types. This document separates what came out
of that into three honestly-different categories, each held to a different bar, because
michi's own `PRINCIPLES.md` sets that bar explicitly (gate 3: *"one tool using a pattern
heavily is one data point, not proof... watch for a second independent confirmation
before building it"*). Monokl is one data point. Where that matters, it's called out.

---

## Category A — genuine bugs, worth fixing regardless of monokl

These aren't "adjust michi to fit monokl" asks. They're correctness/robustness issues any
consumer would hit, found because monokl happened to probe them first.

### A1. `escape_value` deletes newlines instead of escaping them

`crates/michi-toon/src/escape.rs:17,33` — the match arms are `'\n' | '\r' => {}`, i.e. the
character is dropped, not escaped. Verified end-to-end with a real multi-line string: a
TypeScript function's newlines vanish and every line concatenates onto the first, so
```ts
// authenticate the user
export async function login(u: string, p: string) {
```
becomes a single TOON cell where the entire function body ends up *inside* the leading
`//` comment. This isn't a monokl-specific need — it's silent, lossy corruption of any
multi-line string handed to `escape_value`/`escape_value_quoted`, for any consumer.
Gate 1 of your own principles ("rendering, not domain logic... doesn't decide what data
survives") argues this should escape (`\n` → literal `\\n`, or similar), not delete.

### A2. `toon::list()` derives the column set from the first row only

`crates/michi-toon/src/lib.rs` (the `list()` function) takes field names/order from the
**first** item's serialized keys. When `T` has `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "...")]`
fields (a very ordinary pattern — `Option` fields that are usually `None`, empty `Vec`s),
a `None`/empty value in row 1 silently drops that column for *every* row, and the exact

content.text:
monokl is still early. The specs are thorough, the crate has about 7k lines of Rust, and almost none of the actual tool works yet. The crate doesn't compile right now, and the last commit was 2026-09-04, about 7 weeks ago.

**Built so far** (`crates/monokl/src`, 209 commits on `docs/library-session-api-fsl`):
- **Error type and core data types** (`error.rs`, `types.rs`): specs SPEC-001 and SPEC-003 through SPEC-008, with about 3.2k lines of tests in `tests_types.rs`.
- **Query language** (`query/` lexer, parser and plan): SPEC-009.
- **Agent-facing output through michi** (`output/agent.rs`): SPEC-010. The last code work was here, in August.
- **Specced but not built:** SPEC-011 (`ContentHash`). There's no code for it yet.
- **Docs:** the most recent commit adds the library session API spec (`08-library-session-api.md`) and moves the license to FSL-1.1-MIT.

**Blockers and loose ends:**
- **The build fails.** `cargo check` stops with ``registry index was not found in any configuration: `orin-cargo` ``. The `io-errors` dependency points at a private registry, and no `.cargo/config.toml` says where that registry lives. SPEC-004 accepted this on purpose, but it means none of the tests can run until the registry is configured.
- **SPEC-003 is waiting on you.** Its final review step escalated it to a human instead of passing it, and nobody has confirmed it since. The track table in `ACTIVE.md` lists it as GATED anyway.
- **`ACTIVE.md` is out of date.** It still says the query language is "Not started" and doesn't mention SPEC-009, 010 or 011.
- **There's uncommitted work:** edits to 11 spec and plan files (about 726 lines added), plus untracked PLAN-001 and PLAN-003 to PLAN-010, SPEC-009 to SPEC-011, `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md`, `justfile` and `rust-toolchain.toml`.
- **michi bugs to report upstream:** `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md` describes two. `escape_value` deletes newlines instead of escaping them, and `toon::list()` takes its columns from the first row only, so a field that's empty in row 1 is dropped from every row.

**Not started:** the actual tool. That's token counting, text search, ranking, dedup, the token budget, the analyzer trait, the cache and disk storage, the TypeScript analyzer, the indices, the CLI and the napi bindings (tracks 7 to 22). SPEC-002 (cache recovery policy) and the daemon/session mode are in the backlog.

The most useful next steps are configuring the `orin-cargo` registry so the existing tests can run, committing the untracked plans and specs, and starting SPEC-011 (`ContentHash`) or track 7 (token counting).

result: monokl has its core types, error type, query language and michi output layer written, but the build fails on the unconfigured `orin-cargo` registry, SPEC-003 still needs your review, and the actual search, analysis, cache and CLI (tracks 7–22) haven't been started.

Please take a look at callisto and caliper repos. We've been making a lot of changes lately in terms of structure, rust guidance, best practices, crates, tool versions, etc. We would like to learn from these and apply patterns to monokl itself

# Default recipe: run full CI pipeline via moon & just
default: ci

# ── Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# NOTE: intentionally `cargo build --workspace`, not `moon run :build`. Moon's per-project
# `build` task runs `cargo build -p $project` once per crate; every one of those processes
# locks the same shared workspace `target/` directory, so N crates serialize behind that one
# lock instead of actually building in parallel (moonrepo's own Rust handbook documents this).
# A single `--workspace` invocation lets Cargo's own job scheduler parallelize internally,
# with only one process ever holding the lock. Same reasoning applies to `lint`/`test` below,
# which already used this pattern.
build:
    cargo build --workspace

build-release:
    cargo build --release --workspace

# ── Test ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
test:
    cargo test --workspace

# ── Lint & Format ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
check: fmt-check lint

lint:
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

format: fmt

fmt-check:
    cargo fmt --all --check

# ── Affected-only (incremental) ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# For pre-push / incremental CI: scope to only the crates moon's dependency-graph-aware
# affected-detection identifies as changed (real signal a plain `cargo --workspace` can't
# compute), but still issue exactly ONE cargo invocation across all of them -- multiple `-p`
# flags on a single process, not one process per crate -- so this can't reintroduce the same
# build-lock serialization the full-workspace recipes above avoid.
build-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo build "${args[@]}"

    #!/usr/bin/env bash

2. [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md) — the changelog. If something in files 01-04 looks inconsistent, check here before "fixing" it; it's probably already addressed, and the reasoning is recorded.
3. [PRINCIPLES.md](PRINCIPLES.md) — non-goals in particular. Don't propose an embedding-based reranker, a persistent trigram index, or a tree-sitter TS/JS parser — all three were considered and explicitly rejected, with reasons on record.

## Current state

No code exists yet — this is spec-stage. There's no `Cargo.toml`, no build, no test suite to run. If you're asked to implement something, you're implementing _from_ the spec, not extending existing code. Don't invent APIs, types, or command flags that aren't in the spec without flagging that you're doing so — the spec is meant to be reconstructed verbatim, and silent deviation defeats that.

## Code conventions (apply from the first line of code)

- No `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic!()`/`unreachable!()`/`unimplemented!()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — denied by the workspace's own clippy lint table.
- One `thiserror` error enum per crate. Compose new failure modes via `#[from]`/`#[source]`, don't add a `String`-message variant when a structured one is possible.
- `LanguageAnalyzer` implementations must return fully owned data — no arena-borrowed AST nodes, no lifetimes tied to the parser's `Allocator`, ever, in any field of `FileAnalysis`.

Fix it in the spec file, and add an entry to [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md) explaining what was wrong and why the fix is correct — the same pattern already used for the two compile-breaking gaps found there. `cargo nextest` once tests exist. `insta` for snapshots — accept a snapshot change only after confirming the new output is actually correct, not just different.

    - The binding crate has `publish = false`, `crate-type = ["cdylib"]` and build-dep `napi-build = "2"`.
    - tsc-client declares a test-helper binary: `[[bin]] name = "fake-tsc" path = "tests/bin/fake_tsc.rs"`.
  
  ## 3. .cargo / private crates
  - There is **no `.cargo/config.toml`**.
  - No references to `orin-cargo`, `io-errors`, or a `michi` dependency anywhere. `crates/core/src/toon.rs` only says in a doc comment that its TOON renderer is "Inspired by `michi`"; it is a hand-rolled renderer.
  - `deny.toml` `[sources]` sets `unknown-registry = "deny"` and `unknown-git = "deny"`. A private registry would have to be allow-listed there.
  - So caliper offers no pattern for sourcing private crates; that will be new ground for monokl.
  
  ## 4. Format and lint config
  - `.rustfmt.toml`: `edition = "2021"`, `max_width = 120`, `use_small_heuristics = "Max"`.
  - `.clippy.toml`: `msrv = "1.94"`, `too-many-arguments-threshold = 6`, `too-many-lines-threshold = 150`.
  - `deny.toml`:
    - advisories v2 with an empty ignore list.
    - Licenses allow-list: the AGPL, MIT, Apache-2.0 (plus LLVM-exception), ISC, BSD-2 and BSD-3, Unicode-3.0, Zlib, CC0-1.0. Each non-obvious entry has a comment naming the crate that needs it.
    - `multiple-versions = "warn"` with `skip = []`.
  - `.typos.toml`: excludes baselines; `extend-words` with a comment per word.
  - `.oxfmtrc.json`: printWidth 120, no semicolons, single quotes, `proseWrap: "never"`; ignores dist and generated binding files.
  - `.oxlintrc.json`:
    - Plugins: typescript, unicorn, oxc, promise, node.
    - All categories (correctness, suspicious, pedantic, perf, style) are set to `error`, with about 21 rules turned off (no-magic-numbers, sort-keys, one-var, no-null, and so on).
    - A vitest override applies to tests.
  
  ## 5. justfile, moon and CI
  **justfile recipes:**
  - `install-tools`: installs nextest, llvm-cov, machete and mutants, plus llvm-tools-preview.
  - `check-api`: cargo-semver-checks. Not wired into CI until a baseline is published.
  - `install`, `setup` (proto install, pnpm install, `moon sync vcs-hooks`), `clean`.
  - `build`: a single workspace-wide `cargo build`, deliberately not `moon run :build`, because per-crate builds contend for the target/ lock.
  - `test`, `test-rust` (`cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude <napi> --locked` plus `cargo test --doc`), `test-ts`.
  - `coverage threshold=""`: runs `coverage-rust` (`cargo llvm-cov nextest … --lcov`, then `report --fail-under-lines`) and `coverage-ts` (vitest `--coverage.thresholds.lines`). `coverage-html` opens a browser report.
  - `doc-check`: `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps`.
  - `machete`, `mutants` (`cargo mutants --workspace`; on demand only, not part of `ci`), `bench`.
  - `lint`: fmt check, `clippy -D warnings --locked`, oxfmt check on TS and Markdown, oxlint (relaxed for tests).
  - `fmt`, `deny`, `typos`, `zizmor` (`--offline --strict-collection`), `verify-install pm` (scripts/verify-install.sh), `compare`, plus `moon *args` and `cargo *args` passthroughs.
  - `pre-commit`: fmt check, clippy, typos, deny.
  - `ci`: `lint test deny typos zizmor doc-check machete (coverage "90")`.
  
  **moon:** `.moon/workspace.yml` maps the projects and installs a vcs pre-commit hook that just runs `just pre-commit`, so the hook and CI cannot drift. `telemetry: false`.
  
  **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`:** thin jobs that each call `just` (commit 9fb77d85 also dropped change detection).
  - Workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`, a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress, and `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`.
  - Every action is pinned by commit SHA with a version comment, and checkout uses `persist-credentials: false`.
  - Shared setup actions: `orin-dx/actions/setup-rust` and `setup-pnpm-cache` (v1.1), `taiki-e/install-action` for tools, `moonrepo/setup-toolchain`.
  - Jobs:
    - `lint` runs `just lint doc-check machete typos`.
    - `test-rust` runs `just test-rust`.
    - `test-ts` runs on a Node 24/26 matrix.
    - `coverage` runs `just coverage 90` and uploads lcov. This is the 90% line gate for both Rust and TS (commit 1614e837).
    - `install` runs verify-install across node × npm/pnpm.
    - `audit` runs `just deny zizmor`.
    - `changesets` uses `orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-validate@<sha> # callisto@0.8.0`.
    - An aggregate `ci` job (`needs` all of the above, `if: always()`) is the single required check.
  - **Mutation testing is not in CI.** It is the on-demand `just mutants`; mutants.out/ exists locally.
  
  **release.yml:**
  - Callisto jobs in order: release-candidate, then version-pr, then plan (derives a hashed release intent), then build, then execute (publish).
  - The build matrix covers darwin-arm64/x64, linux-x64-gnu, linux-arm64-gnu (via zig) and win32-x64-msvc. Each target runs `pnpm napi build --platform --release --target` plus `cargo build -p cli --target`.
  
  **dependabot.yml:** weekly updates for github-actions, cargo and npm, with groups.
  
  ## 6. Crate choices
  **Workspace dependencies:**
  - oxc_* 0.151 (migrated in 30f803b0), oxc_resolver 11.
  - compact_str 0.10, rustc-hash 2.1, dashmap 6.1, arc-swap 1.9, camino 1.2 (serde1).
  - serde 1.0, serde_json 1.0, rmp-serde 1.3.
  - miette 7.6; the CLI enables the `fancy` feature.
  - rayon 1.12, tokio 1.52, ignore 0.4.
  - clap 4.6 (derive, env, wrap_help), clap_complete, indicatif 0.18, tracing 0.1 with tracing-subscriber 0.3, owo-colors 4.3, watchexec 8.2.
  - napi 3 (napi4) with napi-derive 3; the binding adds the `tokio_rt` feature.
  
  **Dev dependencies:** criterion 0.8, insta 1.48 (json, redactions), pretty_assertions, tempfile 3.20, rstest 0.27, trycmd 1.2, trybuild 1.
  
  **Errors:** library errors use `thiserror = "2"`, declared per-crate in tsc-client rather than in the workspace. The CLI uses miette. Pattern in `crates/tsc-client/src/error.rs`:
  - `#[derive(Debug, Clone, thiserror::Error)] #[non_exhaustive]` enum.
  - Variants are structs carrying context.
  - Non-Clone sources are wrapped as `Arc<io::Error>` with `#[source]` so the error stays Clone.
  
  **Removed in a55a628a:** indexmap, oxc_module_lexer, thiserror (from core), tokio (core), dirs, miette (core), anyhow, clap_mangen, lsp-types, tracing-indicatif, rustc-hash (binding).
  
  ## 7. Guidance docs and rules
  **AGENTS.md convention (a8875cb5):** CLAUDE.md was renamed to AGENTS.md at the root and in each crate (`crates/{core,cli}/AGENTS.md`), linked with `@crates/core/AGENTS.md`.
  
  **Semantic model move (d3254686):** `.claude/semantic-model/` moved to `docs/architecture/` so every agent tool can read it. INDEX.md became `docs/architecture/README.md`, a task-to-file routing table plus cross-cutting invariants, with 7 per-subsystem files that each cite their `Source:` .rs files.
  
  **Root AGENTS.md non-negotiables:**
  1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]`; use `?`. The architecture README extends this to `expect()`.
  2. FxHashMap for internal maps, BTreeMap for JSON output.
  3. CompactString for hot-path names.
  4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()`.
  5. No terminal code in core.
  6. Always emit a `Diagnostic` when degrading.
  
  **Root AGENTS.md, other rules:**
  - One-directional pipeline.
  - `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for the consumer API.
  - Testing discipline:
    - "Sibling-path parity": a function that mirrors an already-tested one needs a test asserting the same contract.
    - "Assert content, not presence": prefer `assert_eq!` on exact values.
  - Writing:
    - Succinct.
    - Never hard-wrap Markdown, commits or PRs.
    - Comments explain only the non-obvious why, carry no history, and fill to 120 columns. Rewriting a comment means re-filling it.
  - Commits:
    - Imperative subject.
    - At most 1–2 sentences of why, no list of changes; skip the body if the subject says it all.
    - In practice they use conventional-commit types with a scope, and add an `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer.
    - CONTRIBUTING also requires GPG signing and `Signed-off-by`.
  
  **CONTRIBUTING.md:**
  - Lays out where code goes: core has no I/O, async or terminal output and must be Send+Sync; cli has no logic; binding is a thin NAPI wrapper that owns tokio.
  - Style:
    - `let…else` for a flat happy path.
    - No wildcard `_` arms on local enums; prefer a full match over `matches!`.
    - Snapshots are reviewed with `cargo insta review`.
  
  **Skills in `.agents/skills/` (mirrored in .claude):**
  - `rust-style`: newtypes over bare types, enums over bool params, explicit destructuring, shadowing instead of `raw_`/`parsed_` prefixes.
  - `rust-types`: checklist for public types — always Debug; Display if shown; Error if a failure; AsRef<str> on string newtypes; `#[non_exhaustive]` on enums that will grow; `#[must_use]`. "Wire or don't define": a new abstraction needs a real call site in the same PR.
  - `rustdoc`: RFC 1574 — first line is one third-person sentence ending in a period; use `///` only, with `//!` for modules; intra-doc links; sections (`# Examples`, `# Panics`, `# Errors`, `# Safety`) only when they carry information; every public fn gets an example; American English.
  - `adr`.
  
  **Crate docs:** `//!` crate docs carry invariants (moved out of an ADR in 49f74a19) — see `crates/tsc-client/src/lib.rs`, "# Session invariants".
  
  **ADRs (`docs/adr/`):**
  - Template `0000-template.md`: `**Status:** Accepted **Date:**`, then Context (2–4 sentences), Decision, Consequences (bullets), and an optional Alternatives considered.
  - 1a9fe7b5 relaxed the Decision section: its shape should fit the decision.
  - README holds:
    - An index with one line per ADR saying what it guards.
    - Two gates before writing one: it must be architectural, and expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.
    - Never edit history; supersede instead. Status is Accepted, Superseded by NNNN, or Deprecated.
    - Banned words: leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, essentially, "in order to", and others.
    - Sentence-case headers, no hard wrap.
  
  **Other docs:** STATUS.md, edge-cases.md, root-cause-analysis.md, archive/ (README-as-index). MIGRATING.md is a user migration guide from react-docgen-typescript with field-by-field tables.
  
  ## 8. Code structure
  - `crates/core/src`: `types/`, `extractor/`, `resolver/`, `pipeline/`, plus flat modules (cache.rs, known.rs, toon.rs, and others).
  - `crates/cli/src`: main.rs (Cli struct and arg structs), `commands/` with one file per subcommand, config.rs, output.rs. All output goes through output.rs; no `println!` in handlers.
  - `crates/tsc-client/src`: client, error, protocol, supervisor, `transport/`.
  - Tests:
    - Core: `crates/core/tests/` with insta `snapshots/`, `compile_fail/` (trybuild), and `benches/` using criterion.
    - Black-box CLI tests (ccee7a67, which took the CLI from 84% to 97% coverage) in `crates/cli/tests/`:
      - `commands.rs` spawns `env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_…")` with a TempDir.
      - `cli_exit_codes.rs` and `lsp_process.rs`.
      - `trycmd.rs` plus `cmd/*.trycmd`.
      - `common/mod.rs` holds shared helpers such as strip_ansi.
    - tsc-client: `tests/common`, `tests/bin/fake_tsc.rs`, and lifecycle_*.rs files.
  - `fixtures/` holds 20 real-library fixture dirs. `apps/validate` is an accuracy comparison tool.
  - `packages/`: `cli` (npm wrapper plus `npm/<platform>/`), `napi` (index.js loader, binding.d.ts, `npm/<platform>/`), `vite-plugin`.
  
  ## 9. Agent tooling layout (ddb1f6c5)
  - `.claude/`: settings.json (Entire hooks on Agent and Skill), `commands/` (check, snapshot), `skills/`, `specs/` (SPEC-*.json spec@1), `worktrees/`.
  - `.agents/skills/`: the shared skill mirror (adr, entire-search, rust-style, rust-types, rustdoc, source-command-check, source-command-snapshot).
  - Entire hooks per tool:
    - `.codex/hooks.json`
    - `.cursor/hooks.json` plus skills/entire-search
    - `.gemini/settings.json` plus skills
    - `.opencode/plugins/entire.ts` plus skills
    - `.github/hooks/entire.json` plus `.github/skills/` (Copilot CLI)
  - Every hook no-ops when `entire` is not on PATH (`sh -c 'if ! command -v entire …; then exit 0; fi; …'`).
  - `.entire/settings.json`: enabled, push checkpoints and sessions, summarize on, telemetry off, checkpoints stored as git-refs. `logs/`, `metadata/` and `tmp/` sit alongside it.
  
  ## 10. Release and versioning
  - LICENSE is AGPL-3.0-or-later; monokl is moving to FSL-1.1-MIT, so deny.toml's allow-list must change accordingly.
  - `.changeset/*.md` uses a frontmatter map of `crate-name: patch|minor|major` followed by a prose consumer-facing summary.
  - `callisto.toml` (callisto 0.8.0; release.yml dropped `--state`/`--recovery`, which were removed in 0.9.0):
    - `[changesets] dir`.
    - `[cascade] mode="out-of-range"`, `bump-severity="patch"`, `peer-escalation`, `preserve-npm-ranges`.
    - One `[[package]]` per `cargo/<name>` or `npm/<name>`, each with `publish-to` and `release-trigger = "changeset"`. The napi crate has `publish-to = []`.
    - `[[fixed-group]]` entries tie the napi crate to its npm wrapper and the cli crate to its npm wrapper.
  - npm platform packages are named `@scope/cli-<platform>`, with `os`/`cpu`, `files` = [binary], `publishConfig.access = public` and a `repository` field (needed for provenance). They are pulled in as optionalDependencies.

content.text:
Both surveys are in. callisto and caliper agree on most conventions, and monokl is missing nearly all of them. Here is what I'd port, then a few choices that are yours to make.

**Both repos do this and monokl doesn't (I'd adopt all of it):**
- **CI:** monokl has no `.github/workflows/` at all. Both siblings use thin jobs that each run a `just` recipe. Actions are pinned to a commit SHA, checkout uses `persist-credentials: false`, and permissions are read-only. They share the `orin-dx/actions/setup-rust` action, gate line coverage at 90%, and add dependabot.
- **justfile:** tests run under `cargo nextest` (monokl's AGENTS.md already says to use it, but the justfile runs `cargo test`). New recipes: `doc-check`, `deny`, `machete`, `typos`, `zizmor`, `coverage 90`, `mutants` (on demand only) and `install-tools`. `ci` would then run all of them.
- **Config files:** `rustfmt.toml` with `max_width = 120`, `.clippy.toml` with `msrv`, and `.typos.toml`. In `deny.toml`, `multiple-versions = "warn"` and unknown registries/git sources denied, with `orin-cargo` and michi's git URL explicitly allowed.
- **Extra lints:**
  - Rust: `unused_must_use` and `let_underscore_drop` set to deny.
  - Clippy: `let_underscore_must_use`, `let_underscore_untyped` and `map_err_ignore` set to deny.
  - monokl's stricter `unwrap`/`expect` deny stays; caliper agrees with it.
- **Docs:**
  - Move `.claude/semantic-model/` to `docs/architecture/`, with a README that maps each task to the right file.
  - Add `docs/adr/` with caliper's template and the rules for when an ADR is warranted.
  - Rewrite AGENTS.md: it still says "No code exists yet". Add the writing rules (120 columns, no hard-wrapped Markdown, comments only for a non-obvious why) and the rule to fix structurally identical bugs in the same change.
  - Copy caliper's `rust-style`, `rust-types` and `rustdoc` skills into `.agents/skills`.
- **Errors and tests:**
  - Errors: `#[non_exhaustive]` error enums with stable miette codes plus help text.
  - CLI tests: black-box tests that run the built binary, plus `trycmd` snapshots.
  - Dev dependency: add `rstest`.

**Where monokl would have to break from its own past choices (these need your call):**
1. **Spec and criterion IDs in code.** callisto's rule is that code never cites them. monokl cites them about 240 times across 9 files in `crates/`.
2. **Toolchain pin.** caliper pins an exact Rust version (1.98.1) in `.prototools` and has no `rust-toolchain.toml`. monokl has both files, with `rust = "1"` and a `wasm32` target.
3. **`orin-cargo` registry.** Neither sibling uses a private registry, so they offer no pattern for it, and monokl still doesn't build without one.
4. **Dependency versions.** oxc 0.128 → 0.151, dashmap 5 → 6 and criterion 0.7 → 0.8. These versions are locked in SPEC-004, so bumping them means correcting that spec too.

I'm keeping monokl's edition 2024 even though both siblings use 2021; there's no reason to go back. monokl's cargo features are tied to its specs, so they stay unless you say otherwise.

1	# Dependency updates. Every ecosystem is grouped into a single routine PR per
2	# week so the queue stays reviewable, with security updates kept in their own
3	# group so an advisory fix is never hidden inside a large routine bump.
4	#
5	# `cooldown` deliberately lags fresh releases: this repo pins GitHub Actions
6	# by commit SHA, and a week is long enough for a yanked crate or a pulled
7	# action release to surface before it lands in a PR here.
8	version: 2
9	
10	updates:
11	  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
12	    directory: /
13	    schedule:
14	      interval: weekly
15	    cooldown:
16	      default-days: 7
17	    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
18	    groups:
19	      routine-actions:
20	        applies-to: version-updates
21	        patterns: ["*"]
22	      security-actions:
23	        applies-to: security-updates
24	        patterns: ["*"]
25	
26	  - package-ecosystem: cargo
27	    directory: /
28	    schedule:
29	      interval: weekly
30	    cooldown:
31	      default-days: 7
32	    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
33	    groups:
34	      # The oxc_* crates are released in lockstep and their minor releases
35	      # carry breaking API changes; keeping them in one PR means the
36	      # extractor and resolver are updated together or not at all.
37	      oxc:
38	        applies-to: version-updates
39	        patterns: ["oxc_*"]
40	      routine-cargo:
41	        applies-to: version-updates
42	        patterns: ["*"]
43	        exclude-patterns: ["oxc_*"]
44	      security-cargo:
45	        applies-to: security-updates
46	        patterns: ["*"]

49	    directory: /

51	      interval: weekly

53	      default-days: 7
54	    open-pull-requests-limit: 3

install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest --locked
    cargo install cargo-llvm-cov --locked
    cargo install cargo-machete --locked
    cargo install cargo-mutants --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Check the public Rust API for accidental SemVer breaks against the last
# published version. Not wired into `just ci` yet — there is no published
# baseline to diff against until v0.1.0's first real crates.io release ships.
# Install with `cargo install cargo-semver-checks --locked` once needed.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

# Install all dependencies
install:
    pnpm install
    cargo fetch

# Build all projects. Rust crates build via one workspace-wide cargo
# invocation, not `moon run :build` — that fans out one `cargo build -p`
# per crate, and every one of those processes contends for the same
# target/ file lock, serializing what moon's own scheduler thinks is
# parallel work (confirmed via `Blocking waiting for file lock` in verbose
# output). napi/vite-plugin have no such lock to contend over, so moon
# still orchestrates those directly.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi
    moon run napi:build vite-plugin:build
    cargo build --release

# Run all tests (Rust + TypeScript)
test: test-rust test-ts

# Run Rust tests (via nextest, which doesn't run doctests — paired
# with `cargo test --doc` to cover those too)
test-rust:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Run TypeScript tests
test-ts:
    pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin test

# Pack the npm packages and check napi arrives only as vite-plugin's transitive dependency (pm: npm or pnpm)
verify-install pm="pnpm":
    scripts/verify-install.sh {{ pm }}

# Run benchmarks
bench:
    cargo bench --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Rust and TypeScript line coverage; with a threshold, fails if either is below it
coverage threshold="": (coverage-rust threshold) (coverage-ts threshold)

# Rust coverage: writes lcov.info and prints the summary before enforcing the threshold
coverage-rust threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# TypeScript coverage: prints the summary and writes packages/vite-plugin/coverage/lcov.info
coverage-ts threshold="":
    pnpm --filter @oxc-react-docgen/vite-plugin exec vitest run --coverage {{ if threshold != "" { "--coverage.thresholds.lines=" + threshold } else { "" } }}

# Rust coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked --html --open

# Documentation build check (warnings, including broken intra-doc links,
# treated as errors)
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

# Unused-dependency check
machete:
    cargo machete

# Mutation testing sweep — slow, run on demand, not part of `just ci`
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi

ts_src := "'packages/vite-plugin/src/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/tests/**/*.ts' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src/**/*.ts'"
ts_src_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/src' 'packages/vite-plugin/vitest.config.ts' 'packages/napi/*.d.ts' 'packages/cli/bin/**/*.js' 'apps/validate/src'"
ts_tests_only := "'packages/vite-plugin/tests'"
md_src := "'**/*.md' '!node_modules/**' '!target/**' '!dist/**'"

# Lint and format check
lint:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt --check {{md_src}}
    pnpm exec oxlint {{ts_src_only}}
    pnpm exec oxlint -A pedantic -A perf -A style -A unicorn/consistent-function-scoping -A vitest/require-mock-type-parameters --vitest-plugin {{ts_tests_only}}

# Format code
fmt:
    cargo fmt
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{ts_src}}
    pnpm exec oxfmt {{md_src}}

# Check licenses, advisories, and banned crates
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Check for typos
typos:
    typos

# Lint GitHub Actions workflows for permission, credential, and supply-chain
# issues. --strict-collection fails on a workflow it cannot parse instead of
# skipping it, so a malformed file can never pass by being ignored.
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Everything the moon-managed pre-commit hook runs. `.moon/workspace.yml`
# calls this recipe rather than repeating the commands, so the hook and
# `just ci` can't drift apart.
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --exclude oxc-react-docgen-napi --locked -- -D warnings
    typos
    cargo deny check

# Everything the CI jobs run, minus the Node version matrix and verify-install
ci: lint test deny typos zizmor doc-check machete (coverage "90")

# Run moon compare task (accuracy vs react-docgen + react-docgen-typescript)
compare:
    moon run validate:compare

# Clean build artifacts
clean:
    moon clean
    cargo clean
    rm -rf node_modules

# Setup toolchain via proto
setup:
    proto install
    pnpm install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Run moon commands
moon *args:
    moon {{args}}

# Run cargo commands
cargo *args:
    cargo {{args}}

# NNNN. Short, decision-shaped title

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** YYYY-MM-DD

## Context

What forced this? The constraint, not the backstory. 2-4 sentences.

## Decision

What we're doing, stated plainly. A paragraph if it's one thing; a short paragraph plus bullets if it splits into a few discrete parts. Match the shape to the decision — don't pad a simple one or cram a multi-part one into a single block.

## Consequences

What this costs and what it buys. Bullets.

-
-

## Alternatives considered (optional)

Only if something else was a real contender. Name it and say why it lost — don't list every option that was never serious.
# Architecture Decision Records

Short, dated records of _architectural_ decisions — ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc, not a place to explain what the code does — comments and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already do that.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Parse with OXC instead of the TypeScript compiler](0001-oxc-over-typescript-compiler.md) — do not add a type-checking pass to the default path. The opt-in backend is 0006.
- [2. Hand-write Serialize/Deserialize for PropType instead of deriving it](0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md) — do not derive them on `PropType` or `CollectedType`.
- [3. Cache the DTS parse cache with positional (not named) MessagePack](0003-positional-msgpack-cache-encoding.md) — do not reorder, insert or remove `SourceData` fields without bumping `CACHE_SCHEMA_VERSION`.
- [4. Defer full type-checker integration](0004-defer-type-checker-integration.md) — superseded by 0006.
- [5. Contain panics at a single, per-item boundary](0005-panic-containment-boundary.md) — route anything reachable from a rayon `.map()`, a `DocgenPlugin` hook or a NAPI entry point through `contain_panic`.
- [6. Run the TypeScript backend as a second resolver](0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md) — do not patch `Opaque` leaves, give `crates/core` a compiler process or I/O, or route the backend through NAPI.


Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects one of: system structure (module/crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR.

Good candidates:

- Choosing OXC over the TypeScript compiler — a technology choice that shapes the whole extraction pipeline
- A serialization format with a hidden constraint (msgpack's positional encoding) — a data contract other code depends on
- Dropping a dependency, or an approach that was tried and abandoned

Not ADR material:

- A single function's algorithm choice, confined to that function — that's a code comment
- A bug fix — commit message, and if it's the kind of thing that could recur, a line in `rdt-coverage.md`
- A behavior-preserving refactor — commit message is enough
- A naming or style convention — that's `AGENTS.md` or a lint rule
- Anything already obvious from the code or from `AGENTS.md`'s non-negotiables
- Per-user preferences, workflow notes and tool quirks — that's agent memory

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by 000X`. Don't rewrite the old file to look like you knew all along.
- **Status** is one of: `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it short. If the technical depth doesn't fit on a screen, split it into its own doc and link it — see `0006-semantic-backend-as-second-resolver.md` pointing at `type-checker-integration.md` instead of inlining it.

## Writing it

Write like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder, not presenting it to a committee. Don't hard-wrap paragraphs at a fixed column — one line per paragraph, let the editor soft-wrap. Every other doc in this repo already does this; hard-wrapping just makes future diffs noisy when a sentence gets edited.

**Cut the filler.** If a sentence still means the same thing without a word, delete the word.

| Instead of | Write |
| --- | --- |
| "It's worth noting that this decision was made in order to leverage OXC's robust parsing capabilities" | "OXC parses in parallel with no type-checking pass" |
| "This represents a significant improvement in performance" | "32ms instead of several seconds" |
| "We decided to essentially utilize a positional encoding approach" | "We use positional encoding" |
| "In conclusion, this architecture provides a solid foundation going forward" | (delete — you already said the thing) |

**Banned by default:** _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._ If one is genuinely the precise technical word for something, fine — but check first.

**Concrete beats vague.** Name the file, the number, the benchmark. "Slow" is not a fact; "several seconds on a mid-size design system" is.

**Active voice, plain structure.** "We chose X because Y" beats "X was chosen due to Y considerations." Sentence-case headers, not Title Case.

**Show the trade-off, not just the win.** A decision with no downside isn't a decision, it's a fact. Say what it costs.

**Structure isn't fixed.** A paragraph, a paragraph plus bullets, a short table — whatever makes it scannable in one pass. `0006`'s Decision section is an intro line plus three bullets because it's three real choices; don't force that into one paragraph, and don't add sections or padding a one-line decision doesn't need.

## What good looks like

Read `0002-manual-serialize-for-prop-type.md` — a real bug behind it, a real number (`recursion_limit = 2048`), a real consequence, four sections, no throat-clearing.

# List available commands
default:
    @just --list

# Install the cargo tools the recipes below use
install-tools:
    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked
    rustup component add llvm-tools-preview

# Install the pinned toolchain and the moon-managed git hooks
setup:
    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

# Build the workspace. One `cargo --workspace` invocation, not `moon run :build`: per-crate cargo processes all
# contend for the same target/ lock and serialize.
build:
    cargo build --workspace --locked

build-release:
    cargo build --workspace --release --locked

# Run tests with nextest, plus doctests, which nextest does not run
test:
    cargo nextest run --workspace --all-features --locked
    cargo test --doc --workspace --all-features --locked

# Line coverage; with a threshold, fails below it
coverage threshold="":
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --lcov --output-path lcov.info
    cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only
    if [[ -n "{{ threshold }}" ]]; then
      cargo llvm-cov report --summary-only --fail-under-lines "{{ threshold }}"
    fi

# Coverage report, opened in the browser
coverage-html:
    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

# Format check and clippy, with and without default features
lint:
    cargo fmt --all --check
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
    cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --no-default-features --locked -- -D warnings

# Clippy on the crates moon reports as affected, in one cargo invocation
lint-affected:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    projects=$(moon query projects --affected | jq -r '.projects[].id')
    if [ -z "$projects" ]; then exit 0; fi
    args=()
    for p in $projects; do args+=(-p "$p"); done
    cargo clippy "${args[@]}" --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings

fmt:
    cargo fmt --all

# Documentation build, with warnings (including broken intra-doc links) as errors
doc-check:
    RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace --all-features --locked

# Licenses, advisories, bans and sources
deny:
    cargo deny check

# Unused dependencies
machete:
    cargo machete

typos:
    typos

# Workflow audit for permission, credential and supply-chain issues
zizmor:
    zizmor --offline --strict-collection .

# Mutation testing. Slow, so on demand only, not part of `just ci`.
mutants:
    cargo mutants --workspace

# Public API SemVer check against the last published version. Not in `just ci` until a first release exists.
check-api:
    cargo semver-checks check-release

clean:
    moon clean 2>/dev/null || true
    cargo clean

# Run by the moon-managed pre-commit hook
pre-commit:
    cargo fmt --all --check
    typos

# Run by the moon-managed pre-push hook
pre-push: pre-commit lint-affected

# Everything the CI jobs run
ci: lint test doc-check deny machete typos zizmor (coverage "90")

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

# Each job runs `just` recipes, so `just ci` locally does what CI does.
jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: clippy,rustfmt
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-machete,typos
      - run: just lint doc-check machete typos

  test:
    name: Test / ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest
      - run: just test

  msrv:
    name: MSRV
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: msrv
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}
      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest,cargo-llvm-cov
      - run: just coverage 90
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        if: always()
        with:
          name: coverage
          path: lcov.info
          retention-days: 14

  audit:
    name: Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@94c31af3204a9f15ab40b35ad084410b905bbc73 # v2.87.17
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-deny,zizmor@1.29.0
      - run: just deny zizmor

  # The one check to require in branch protection.
  ci:
    name: CI
    needs: [lint, test, msrv, coverage, audit]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - if: contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') || contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')
        run: exit 1

# Grouped weekly updates, with security updates in their own group so an advisory fix is never hidden in a routine
# bump. The cooldown lets a yanked crate or pulled action release surface before it lands here.
version: 2

updates:
  - package-ecosystem: github-actions
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 3
    groups:
      routine-actions:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
      security-actions:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

  - package-ecosystem: cargo
    directory: /
    schedule:
      interval: weekly
    cooldown:
      default-days: 7
    open-pull-requests-limit: 5
    groups:
      # oxc_* minor releases carry breaking API changes and ship in lockstep, so they update together.
      oxc:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["oxc_*"]
      routine-cargo:
        applies-to: version-updates
        patterns: ["*"]
        exclude-patterns: ["oxc_*"]
      security-cargo:
        applies-to: security-updates
        patterns: ["*"]

# Architecture

Topic docs for monokl's subsystems. Read the one your task touches, not all of them. Each distills the `docs/spec/` sections it cites and the edge-case findings that change what an implementer must do; where code exists, the code and its tests are authoritative and the doc should be kept in step with them.

## Task to file

| You are working on | Read |
| --- | --- |
| `error.rs`, `file_io.rs`, `MonoklError`, any `Result<T>` return | [error-taxonomy.md](error-taxonomy.md) |
| `types.rs`, `SymbolEntry`, `Visibility`, `LanguageId`, `CodeBlock` | [core-types.md](core-types.md) |
| `query/`, ranking, BM25, tie-breaking, determinism | [query-and-ranking.md](query-and-ranking.md) |
| The in-memory and disk cache, content hash vs. mtime | [cache-architecture.md](cache-architecture.md) |
| `LanguageAnalyzer`, `AnalyzerRegistry`, capability and precision gating | [language-analyzer-contract.md](language-analyzer-contract.md) |
| Daemon and session mode, `PrecisionUpgrader`, `PrecisionLedger` (not v0.1.0) | [daemon-lifetimes.md](daemon-lifetimes.md) |

## Cross-cutting invariants

- One `thiserror` error enum for the crate, `MonoklError`; file I/O failures are `FileIoError` wrapped transparently.
- `camino::Utf8Path` everywhere a path appears, except where the path is by definition not UTF-8.
- `FxHashMap`/`FxHashSet` for internal hot-path maps; `BTreeMap` for anything serialized, because output order must be deterministic.
- Analyzers return fully owned data. No arena-borrowed AST node outlives the parse.

## Elsewhere

- Decisions with a credible alternative: [`docs/adr/`](../adr/README.md).
- The full spec and its decision log: [`docs/spec/`](../spec/README.md), [`05-research-and-decisions.md`](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md).
- The edge-case audit these docs draw on: [`07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md`](../spec/07-edge-cases-and-failure-modes.md).

10-100x faster than react-docgen-typescript. OXC parses TypeScript/TSX; we extract React component props and emit RDT-compatible JSON via `--format rdt`. See `docs/STATUS.md` for current state and known gaps.

## Non-negotiables

1. No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?`
2. `FxHashMap` for internal maps; `BTreeMap` for JSON-output maps
3. `CompactString` for type/prop names in hot paths
4. No AST refs escape `parse_file()` — allocator is local per call
5. No terminal/display code in `crates/core`
6. Always emit `Diagnostic` when degrading — never fail silently

## Architecture

```
OXC parse → SourceData (extractor/) → GlobalSourceData (pipeline/) → ComponentEntry (resolver/) → ExtractionOutput
```

No reverse dependencies. `pub(crate)` for implementation modules; `pub` only for consumer-facing API (`pipeline/`, `types/`, `react_types`).

See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the full pipeline/crate-graph overview, and `docs/architecture/` for per-subsystem invariants and known gaps (pipeline orchestration, extractor, resolver, types, serialization, CLI, NAPI binding) — start at `docs/architecture/README.md`.

## Decisions

Read `docs/adr/README.md` before changing the parser choice, `PropType` serialization, the DTS cache format, panic containment or the semantic backend. Reversing an ADR needs a new ADR.

## Testing discipline

Two habits that repeatedly caught real bugs during the 2026-08-12 spec-validation pass (a stale-by-one-edit watch mode, always-zero watch stats — both had zero test coverage despite extensive existing suites):

1. **Sibling-path parity.** When a function parallels an already-tested one (e.g. `WatchSession::update_file` mirrors `extract()`'s resolve/panic-containment logic; `create_session`'s guard boundary mirrors `initialize_session`/`extract_file_incremental`'s), the new path needs a test asserting the _same_ contract, not just "it runs without error." A sibling path is exactly where coverage silently lapses.
2. **Assert content, not presence.** Prefer `assert_eq!` against an exact expected value over `contains(...)`/`is_some()`/liveness checks wherever the cost is comparable. A test asserting "component X exists" survives X's props resolving to stale or wrong data; a test asserting X's exact prop set does not.

## Crate guide

- `crates/core` — pure extraction logic; @crates/core/AGENTS.md
- `crates/cli` — clap CLI, no logic; @crates/cli/AGENTS.md
- `crates/binding` — thin NAPI wrapper, delegates to core

## Writing and commits

- Succinct: short sentences, bullets, tables. No backstory, hedging or filler. Banned words are in `docs/adr/README.md`.
- Never hard-wrap Markdown, commit messages or PR descriptions: one line per paragraph.
- Comments: only the non-obvious why, no history (the commit records it). Fill to 120 columns (`.rustfmt.toml`). Rewriting a comment block counts as writing it: re-fill and cut it, don't inherit the old wrapping.
- Commits: imperative subject, at most one or two sentences of why, no list of what changed, no "This commit...". Skip the body when the subject says it all.
---
name: rust-style
description: Apply when writing or modifying Rust code in this project.
---

**Goal:** Code correct by construction, readable under churn, performant in hot paths.

## Project-specific decisions

These are non-negotiables, not preferences:

- Internal maps: `FxHashMap`. JSON-output maps: `BTreeMap` (deterministic key ordering).
- Type/prop names: `CompactString` — avoids heap allocation for strings ≤24 bytes.
- No `unwrap()` outside `#[cfg(test)]` — use `?` and let callers decide what to do with failure.

## Control flow

`let...else` keeps the happy path flat:

```rust
let Some(entry) = map.get(key) else { return None };
let Ok(parsed) = input.parse::<u32>() else { continue };
```

## Matching

No wildcards — a compile error on unhandled variants is a feature:

```rust
match status { Status::Ok => .., Status::Err => .. }  // compiler tells you when Status grows
match status { Status::Ok => .., _ => .. }             // silently misses new variants
```

Full `match` over `matches!` for the same reason.

## Types

Newtypes when a bare type allows confusion. Enums when a bool parameter hides intent:

```rust
struct ScopedKey(CompactString);         // not: String
enum Visibility { Public, Private }      // not: is_public: bool
```

Explicit destructuring gets compiler errors when structs change:

```rust
let ComponentEntry { display_name, file_path, .. } = entry;
```

## Naming

Shadow variables through transformations — no `raw_`/`parsed_`/`trimmed_` prefixes:

```rust
let path = args.path;
let path = path.canonicalize()?;
let path = path.join("config.toml");
```

## Comments

Only when the WHY is non-obvious: a hidden constraint, a workaround, a non-obvious invariant. Not what the code does.
---
name: rust-types
description: Apply when defining new public structs or enums.
---

**Goal:** Every public type is immediately usable, visible in error messages, and extendable without semver breaks.

## Checklist before merging a new `pub struct` or `pub enum`

- `#[derive(Debug)]` — always
- `impl Display` — if it appears in messages, CLI output, or diagnostic text
- `impl std::error::Error` — if it represents a failure condition
- `impl AsRef<str>` — on string newtypes
- `#[non_exhaustive]` — on enums that will gain variants; adding one without this is a semver break
- `#[must_use]` — on functions whose return value the caller must not silently drop

## Wire or don't define

A new abstraction needs a real call site in the same PR — not a follow-up ticket. An unused type adds noise and false confidence. If the use case isn't clear yet, leave a note in the doc instead.

# 1. Keep FileIoError in monokl instead of a shared io-errors crate

**Status:** Accepted **Date:** 2026-10-21

## Context

The spec (`01-core-architecture.md` §1 and §27) puts `FileIoError` in a separate `io-errors` crate, pulled from a private `orin-cargo` registry. That crate was never written or published, and no `.cargo/config.toml` defines the registry, so `cargo metadata` failed at manifest parse and monokl could not build or run a single test.

## Decision

`FileIoError` is the `monokl::file_io` module, with the spec's §27 contents unchanged. `MonoklError::Io` wraps it with `#[error(transparent)]` and `#[from]`. There is no private registry: dependencies come from crates.io, or by pinned git revision from an `orin-dx` repository allowed in `deny.toml`.

## Consequences

- monokl builds and tests with no out-of-repo setup.
- Another orin-dx tool that wants the same type cannot depend on it without depending on monokl. When a second tool needs it, it moves to a shared crate, under michi's own "second independent data point" rule.
- `docs/spec/01-core-architecture.md` §1 and §27 still describe the separate crate and need a matching correction.

## Alternatives considered

- **A new michi crate.** michi renders agent-facing responses; its principles keep domain logic out, and a file I/O error with a path is domain logic. One consumer is also one data point, which michi's principles say is not enough to add a primitive.
- **`crates/io-errors` in this workspace.** It would be publishable on its own, but it adds a crate to version and release for one 70-line enum with one consumer. callisto merged its crates down to four for the same overhead.

# Architecture decision records

Short, dated records of architectural decisions: ones that shape system structure, boundaries, or contracts other code depends on. Not a changelog, not a design doc. Comments, `ARCHITECTURE.md` and `docs/architecture/` explain what the code does.

The spec's own decision log, [`docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md`](../spec/05-research-and-decisions.md), records how the spec was reached. ADRs record decisions made since, including any that depart from the spec.

## Index

One line per ADR, with what it guards. Add a line when you add an ADR.

- [1. Keep FileIoError in monokl instead of a shared io-errors crate](0001-file-io-error-lives-in-monokl.md): do not reintroduce a private registry; move `FileIoError` to a shared crate only when a second tool needs it.

Changing any of these needs a new ADR.

## When to write one

Two gates, both required:

1. **Architectural.** It affects system structure (module or crate boundaries, how components interact), a dependency or technology choice that ripples across the codebase, a data format or contract other code depends on, or a cross-cutting constraint (performance model, correctness discipline, security model).
2. **Expensive to reverse and not obvious from the code.** If it gets reverted in a year, what breaks, and would anyone know why?

If either answer is no, it's not an ADR. A single function's algorithm is a code comment; a bug fix or refactor is a commit message; a naming or style convention belongs in `AGENTS.md` or a lint.

## Format

One file per decision: `docs/adr/NNNN-short-title.md`, numbered sequentially, never reused. Copy `0000-template.md` to start.

- **Never edit history.** If a decision changes, write a new ADR and mark the old one's status `Superseded by NNNN`.
- **Status** is one of `Accepted`, `Superseded by NNNN`, `Deprecated`.
- Keep it to a screen. Put technical depth in `docs/architecture/` and link it.

## Writing it

Write it like you're explaining it to the next engineer over their shoulder. One line per paragraph, no hard wrapping. Sentence-case headers.

- Cut filler. If a sentence means the same without a word, delete the word.
- Banned by default: _leverage, utilize, robust, seamless, cutting-edge, essentially, basically, in order to, it's worth noting, it is important to note, at the end of the day._
- Concrete beats vague. Name the file, the number, the command.
- Active voice. "We chose X because Y."
- Show the trade-off. A decision with no downside is a fact, not a decision.

  "crates/michi-core",
  "crates/michi-pipeline",
  "packages/michi-node"
]
resolver = "2"

[workspace.package]
# No shared `version`: Callisto writes each crate's version itself and keeps michi-core, michi-pipeline and the npm
# package equal through its fixed group (callisto.toml). CI's version-sync job checks they agree.
edition      = "2021"
rust-version = "1.96"
license      = "FSL-1.1-MIT"
repository   = "https://github.com/orin-dx/michi"
authors      = ["Orin DX"]
homepage     = "https://orin-dx.com/tools/michi/"

[workspace.dependencies]
# Exact pin: workspace crates release in lockstep, so a mixed set must never resolve.
michi-core  = { path = "crates/michi-core", version = "=0.3.1" }
thiserror   = "2"
compact_str = "0.8"
serde       = { version = "1.0.228", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json  = { version = "1.0.150", features = ["preserve_order"] }
schemars    = "0.8"
miette      = "7"
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["time"] }

[profile.release]
opt-level     = 3
lto           = "thin"
codegen-units = 1

[profile.bench]
inherits = "release"
debug    = true

# Single source of truth for unsafe_code -- every crate in this workspace
# opts in via `[lints]`/`workspace = true`, replacing a hand-copied
# `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` at the top of every lib.rs. Stays "deny" (not
# "forbid") so the napi boundary's local `#![allow(unsafe_code)]` can still
# override it -- see CLAUDE.md's "No unsafe outside napi boundary".
#
# missing_docs / clippy::unwrap_used / clippy::expect_used /
# clippy::disallowed_types stay as per-crate `#![warn(...)]` inner
# attributes in each lib.rs instead of living here: `[lints]` applies to
# every target in a package (every integration test, bench, and example,
# not just the lib target), and those four lints are specifically meant to
# apply to library code only -- CLAUDE.md's "no unwrap/expect in lib code"
# rule was never meant to cover benches/examples, and doc-coverage doesn't
# make sense for internal test binaries. unsafe_code is the one lint here
# with no such exception (nothing outside the documented napi boundary
# should ever contain unsafe), so it's the only one safe to centralize.
[workspace.lints.rust]
unsafe_code = "deny"

Yes. monokl now uses `michi-core` 0.3.1 from crates.io instead of a git pin, and `just ci` passes: 271 tests, lint, docs, deny, typos, zizmor, and 98.6% coverage. It's pushed to PR https://github.com/orin-dx/monokl/pull/3, and the PR description is updated.

- **Which crate:** only `michi-core` and `michi-pipeline` are on crates.io. The `michi` name there still belongs to an unrelated project, and the old `michi-toon` and similar crates are now folded into `michi-core`. In `Cargo.toml` I renamed it back to `michi`, so none of monokl's `michi::` paths had to change.
- **No more git sources:** `deny.toml` no longer needs an exception for a git dependency, so anything not from crates.io is now rejected.

**Changes from michi 0.3:**
- **Newline escaping is fixed.** The old michi deleted newlines, which is item A1 in `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md`, and monokl's `cell()` escaped them as a workaround. michi 0.3 escapes them itself, so keeping the workaround would have escaped twice and shown agents a literal `\n` instead of a line break. `cell()` now passes text through unchanged.
- **Null and empty values now look different.** A missing value renders as `null` and an empty string as `""`.
- **A single hint renders on one line**, as `help[1]: …`.
- **Commas in field names are now quoted instead of rejected.** I changed the validation test to use a duplicate field name, which michi still rejects.

The `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md` file in your main checkout may now be out of date. michi's tests suggest A1 and A2 are both fixed in 0.3.

53	### A3. `render_toon`'s row/header arity mismatch is a `debug_assert!`, not a handled error
54	
55	`crates/michi-toon/src/render.rs:142` — a row whose length doesn't match the header count
56	panics in debug builds via `debug_assert!`, silently mismatches in release. For a library
57	meant to be embedded in multiple production CLI/agent tools, a panic path reachable from
58	malformed-but-plausible caller input (not just programmer error) is a rough edge —
59	monokl's own adapter design works around this with a const-generic trait that makes arity
60	a compile-time guarantee, but that's a caller-side mitigation, not a library-level fix.
61	Worth considering whether `render_toon` should return `Result` (or call `.validate()`
62	internally) instead of trusting the caller to have gotten arity right.
63	
64	### A4. `AgentResponse::toon_body()` swallows `validate()` failure into the body, with `is_error: false`
65	
66	If `ToonOptions::validate()` fails, the failure text gets written into the *body* of an
67	otherwise-successful-looking response (`isError: false`, `exit_code` unset/0). An agent
68	consuming this sees a normal-looking success response whose content happens to be an
69	error message — worse than a normal error, since nothing signals "don't trust this
70	payload." Either call `.validate()` automatically before rendering and surface real
71	failures as real errors, or make this failure mode visible in `is_error`.
72	
73	### A5. `DomainError::render()`/`render_hints`/`append_hints` don't sanitize newlines
74	
75	Unlike the TOON path, `error.rs`'s `render()` and `hints.rs`'s `append_hints` write
76	`message`/hint text raw into a line-oriented `key: value` / `help[N]:` block. A message or
77	hint containing a newline (e.g. relaying multi-line subprocess stderr, which is common —
78	git, a linter, a compiler) produces a malformed, unparseable block: an orphan line with no
79	`key:` prefix. Verified live:
80	```
81	error: external_failure
82	message: git_failed: git rev-parse failed: fatal: ambiguous argument 'nope'
83	Use '--' to separate paths          ← orphan line, breaks any KV parser
84	exit_code: 1
85	```
86	Same class of bug as A1, in a different module — worth a single shared sanitization pass
87	applied consistently across every render path, not just TOON's.
88	
89	---
90	
91	## Category B — already michi's own stated direction, monokl ready to be the evidence
92	
93	Not new asks. `PRINCIPLES.md`'s own "split the decision from the signal" section already
94	designs this and flags it explicitly as **not yet implemented**:

96	```rust
97	pub struct TruncationOutcome<T> { pub kept: Vec<T>, pub total_before: usize, pub truncated: bool }
98	pub fn truncate_by_count<T>(items: Vec<T>, max: usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
99	pub fn truncate_by_bytes<T>(items: Vec<T>, max_bytes: usize, size_of: impl Fn(&T) -> usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
100	```
101	
102	monokl's own `budget.rs` (spec'd, not yet implemented) needs exactly this shape: cap a
103	`Vec<RankedBlock>` by a size metric and report what got cut, in a consistent agent-
104	readable form. The one difference is the metric — monokl caps by **LLM token count**
105	(tiktoken/o200k_base), not byte length. But `size_of: impl Fn(&T) -> usize` already
106	accepts *any* caller-supplied sizing function — feed it a token-counting closure and
107	`truncate_by_bytes` (or a `truncate_by_size`/generically-named variant) already covers
108	monokl's case with zero new michi surface. monokl isn't asking for something new here —
109	it's offering to be the real-consumer evidence this sketch has been waiting for.
110

113	## Category C — genuinely cross-tool ergonomic gap, not proven by monokl alone but structurally likely to recur
114	
115	### C1. No helper for building a `DomainError` from a `thiserror`-based domain error while preserving its cause chain
116	
117	`DomainError`'s `impl std::error::Error for DomainError {}` is empty — `source()` returns
118	`None` unconditionally, and thiserror's `Display` doesn't include `#[source]` either. So
119	any consumer converting their own crate's `thiserror` enum (the shape monokl's own
120	`AGENTS.md` mandates — "one thiserror error enum per crate" — and plausibly true of every
121	other orin-axi tool too, if they follow the same convention) into a `DomainError` has to
122	manually walk `Error::source()` themselves to avoid silently dropping the cause chain.
123	monokl's adapter had to write this from scratch:
124	
125	```rust
126	fn chain_lines(e: &dyn std::error::Error) -> Vec<String> { /* walk .source(), one line per link */ }
127	```
128	
129	This isn't monokl-specific — it's the generic shape of "I have a thiserror enum, I want a
130	`DomainError` that doesn't lose the cause chain," which is plausibly every consumer's
131	first integration step. Unlike the `ErrorCode` question below, this doesn't require
132	michi to know anything about monokl's domain — it's a pure mechanical utility
133	(`DomainError::from_error_chain(e: &dyn std::error::Error, code: ErrorCode) -> Self`, or
134	similar) that would generalize immediately. Flagging this as the strongest Category-C
135	candidate — closer to Category A than a "maybe" in spirit, since it doesn't require any

Both open items are worth building, and both are small. B (truncation reporting) is the stronger case: michi's own `PRINCIPLES.md` already sketches the API, and caliper has hand-rolled the same signal. C1 (keeping an error's cause chain) is a mechanical helper, but so far only monokl has needed it.

## B. `TruncationOutcome`: report what got cut, however it was cut

**Problem.** Every tool that caps a list decides for itself which items survive. Telling the agent what was dropped is a separate job, and right now each tool does it its own way:
- monokl's spec (Part 8 §9.1, `08-library-session-api.md:487`) has core report `items_returned` and `items_total`, and leaves the output layer to render the "there is more" signal.
- caliper hand-rolls a `"...(+N)"` marker (`truncate_with_indicator`, `caliper/crates/core/src/toon.rs:97`).

That's two independent tools inventing the same signal, which is the evidence `PRINCIPLES.md` gate 3 asks for. Say so in the PR.

**Current michi state.**
- `PRINCIPLES.md:45-70` ("Split the decision from the signal") sketches this API, but it isn't implemented.
- `truncate.rs` only truncates within a string (`truncate`, `truncate_inline`), not lists.
- `AgentResponse` and `ToonOptions` already have `total_count`, which renders `totalCount: N`. That covers half the signal.

**Proposed API.** This is the sketch from `PRINCIPLES.md`, with three changes:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
pub struct TruncationOutcome<T> {
    pub kept: Vec<T>,
    pub total_before: usize,
}

impl<T> TruncationOutcome<T> {
    /// For callers with their own selection heuristic: wrap whatever they kept.
    pub fn new(kept: Vec<T>, total_before: usize) -> Self;
    pub fn truncated(&self) -> bool { self.kept.len() < self.total_before }
    pub fn omitted(&self) -> usize;
    /// `None` when nothing was cut.
    pub fn hint(&self, guidance: impl Into<String>) -> Option<Hint>;
}

pub fn truncate_by_count<T>(items: Vec<T>, max: usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
pub fn truncate_by_size<T>(items: Vec<T>, budget: usize, size_of: impl Fn(&T) -> usize) -> TruncationOutcome<T>;
```

The three changes:
1. **`truncated` is a method, not a field.** A stored `bool` can disagree with `kept.len()` and `total_before`.
2. **There's a `new()` constructor.** `#[non_exhaustive]` stops other crates from building the struct by hand. Without `new()`, a tool with its own heuristic, which is the whole point of the type, couldn't create one.
3. **`truncate_by_size` replaces `truncate_by_bytes`.** `size_of` can measure anything, and monokl's budget is tokens, not bytes.

**Decisions to make (record them in michi's Design Decisions table):**
- **How `truncate_by_size` fills the budget.**
  - *Stop at the first item that doesn't fit:* keeps order, and the rule is easy to explain.
  - *Skip items that don't fit and keep going:* fills the budget more completely, but output order no longer says what was dropped.
  - I'd stop at the first item that doesn't fit; a tool that wants the other behavior uses `new()`.
- **A first item larger than the budget.** Either `kept` is empty with `truncated() == true`, or the first item is always kept. I'd return empty and let the hint explain why.
- **Hint wording.** Something like `showing {kept} of {total}; {guidance}`, with the `guidance` text left to the caller, the same way `truncate` handles its hint. This keeps michi from inventing a flag the calling tool might not have.
- **Wiring into `AgentResponse`.** A `.truncation(&outcome, guidance)` builder that sets `total_count` and appends the hint would keep the two from drifting apart. Check gate 4 first: it overlaps the existing `total_count` field, and that overlap is the reason to have one call set both.

**Tests to write first (michi works test-first):**
- Empty input, zero cap and an exact fit: nothing is cut and `hint()` returns `None`.
- `truncate_by_count` keeps the first N items, in order.
- `truncate_by_size` stops at the first item that doesn't fit, including the oversized-first-item case.
- `size_of` additions saturate rather than overflowing.
- `hint()` produces exact text, checked against string literals.
- `new(kept, total)` for a custom heuristic renders the same hint as the built-in functions.

**How monokl would use it:** the future `budget.rs` would wrap its token-capped `Vec<RankedBlock>` in a `TruncationOutcome`. The output layer would render it, replacing the pre-rendered `truncation_marker` strings that the spec bans from core.

## C1. Keep an error's cause chain when building a `DomainError`

**Problem.** `DomainError` implements the `Error` trait, but `source()` always returns `None` (`error.rs:272`). There's no way to build one from a `thiserror` error without manually walking the `source()` chain. Every consumer that follows the orin-dx "one thiserror enum" rule has to write that loop. monokl did, in `to_domain_error` (`crates/monokl/src/output/agent.rs:638-647`):
1. `message` = the error's own `Display`.
2. Walk `source()` and add each link's `Display` as a hint.
3. Split each link on line breaks (`split_display_lines`, line 680).

**Current michi state.**
- `DomainError` derives `Clone` and, behind a feature flag, `schemars::JsonSchema`.
- `render()` now escapes messages and hints per TOON 4.4. So the line-splitting in step 3 is no longer required for correct output, only a formatting preference.

**Proposed API:**

```rust
impl DomainError {
    /// `message` is `err`'s own Display; each `source()` link's Display becomes a hint, outermost first.
    pub fn from_error(code: ErrorCode, err: &(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)) -> Self;
}
```

**Decisions to make:**
- **Should `source()` work in Rust code too?**
  - **Render-only (the API above):** no new field. The chain survives only in rendered output (the hints).
  - **Also store the cause:** add `source: Option<Arc<dyn Error + Send + Sync>>`. `Arc` keeps `DomainError` cloneable, and `source()` then works for code using it as a Rust error.
    - Costs: it needs `#[schemars(skip)]`, the `Send + Sync` checks in michi-core's `lib.rs` tests need re-checking, and the error constructor needs an owned error (`impl Error + Send + Sync + 'static`).
  - **My recommendation:** ship render-only first. Add the stored cause only when a consumer needs `source()`.
- **Hint per chain link or per line.** monokl does one hint per line. Now that michi escapes line breaks, one hint per link is simpler and loses nothing. Pick one and document it.
- **Message prefix.** monokl prefixes the message with its own code (`walk: …`). Leave that to callers (`from_error(...)`, then edit `.message`), not a parameter.
- **Gate 3 evidence is thin.** Only monokl has hand-written this. callisto and caliper use miette's `#[diagnostic(transparent)]` and don't use michi. If you'd rather not build on one data point, the PR can say this is a mechanical helper with no domain knowledge in it. That was the argument in `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md`, but it's weaker than B's evidence.

**Tests to write first:**
- A two-level `thiserror` chain gives the exact message plus exactly one hint per cause, outermost first.
- An error with no source gives no hints.
- A multi-line cause renders as a single escaped hint.
- With the miette feature on, `help()` includes the chain.

**How monokl would use it:** most of `to_domain_error` collapses to `DomainError::from_error(code, self)` plus monokl's code prefix and recovery hints. `split_display_lines` can then go.

---

Once both ship, delete `MICHI-ADJUSTMENTS.md`; its A items are already fixed in michi 0.3.1. I can file B and C1 as issues on orin-dx/michi with this text if you want them tracked there.
